reason: E1 directly supports the ductility premise by showing that an inverted BCC+B2 microstructure with discrete B2 precipitates in a BCC matrix improves room-temperature ductility. E2 supports that coherent precipitates are thermally activatable and do not drastically reduce strain rate sensitivity, but neither E1 nor E2 provides any evidence that such precipitates act as defect sinks for irradiation damage, which is a key mechanistic premise. The high-temperature strength retention of the BCC phase and the feasibility of aging NbMoTaW to form B2 precipitates are not supported by the cited evidence
premises: A BCC matrix with discrete B2 precipitates improves room-temperature ductility in RHEAs
Nanoscale coherent precipitates can act as defect sinks for irradiation-generated point defects and helium
Coherent precipitates remain thermally activatable and do not severely reduce strain rate sensitivity
The BCC phase can retain high-temperature strength up to 1600 °C in NbMoTaW
Aging can produce a fine dispersion of coherent B2 precipitates in a BCC NbMoTaW matrix
